title: Java Collections: List, Set, Map & HashMap

scenes.line2: What makes List, Set, Map unique?
scenes.say: Ever wonder why interviewers always ask about Java collections? What makes List, Set, and Map so special?

scenes.label: List
scenes.sub: ArrayList is fast for access, LinkedList is fast for insert and delete.
scenes.say: Lists store ordered elements. ArrayList is quick for access, while LinkedList is better for insert and delete.
Sets prevent duplicates. HashSet adds quickly, TreeSet keeps things sorted. Maps store key-value pairs. HashMap gets values fast, TreeMap sorts keys.

rows.b: Java 8+ uses trees for heavy collisions

scenes.say: HashMap uses buckets for storage. Collisions are handled with lists, and since Java eight, trees help when collisions get heavy. It resizes itself to stay fast.

scenes.question: Is HashMap always O(1) for get?
scenes.right: No. Poor hashCode or too many collisions can slow it down.
scenes.say: Is HashMap always constant time for getting values? Not if your hash code is bad or collisions pile up. Watch out for that.
